title: Shared-host turns
current: Each Test Machine keeps one FIFO waiting line (qa_test_machine_waits). A scoped QA plan execution whose host is leased or unhealthy, and a refused manual QA_HOST:<machine> acquire, both join it. Unhealthy means the newer of the host's verification and its last successful golden capture is a failed verification; reset and diagnosis receipts never decide it. A plan case whose host SSH cannot reach (ssh_unavailable: connect timeout, refusal, no route or rejected key) records that failed verification itself and joins the line instead of recording an error verdict; A host with cloud_instance_id is started before SSH is tried (see cloud-power); the operator starts any other stopped host and runs yoke test-machine verify, whose successful release wakes the line. The plan runner prints 'Queued for QA host <machine>, position N of M' with the park command, and the item and run QA-stage wakes teach: if your host is busy, let the plan runner queue you, then park; you'll be woken when it's your turn, with no free-text host hold. A new walk of the same run, stage and shared plan as an aborted walk that held the host takes that walk's place in line, so the recovery resumes next, ahead of unrelated waiters. A plan execution has one place in every line, its first wait's: moving to another host keeps it, and a case needing a host set (method_config.test_machines, unioned only within its own inherit chain) waits on every host at that place and keeps hosts already reserved for it. It takes the set only when every host is free or reserved for it, and is woken once its last host is reserved. A reservation held by an execution still waiting for another host passes to an older waiter on that host, so two sets needing the same hosts in opposite orders both finish. A chain baseline holds exactly its set: a one-host baseline holds only its host. Every release of a healthy host, including yoke claims work release by claim id, reserves it for the oldest live waiter and wakes that session; the waiter's next acquire consumes the turn. A yoke test-machine reset or verify the holder runs on a turn reserved for its plan execution borrows that turn without consuming it, so the turn stays reserved through submit or abort and the plan's own yoke qa plan run takes the host while later waiters keep waiting. A session that just used a host keeps it as a 120-second same-session hold-over: a yoke test-machine exec (or desktop access, or browser sign-in) released onto an empty line, so its preflight's next yoke qa case run wins over a later session's plan run, while a session already queued still outranks it; and every host an execution held or had reserved when its own session aborts it (for example after served_build_changed), so its rerun keeps the turn. The exec names the hold-over and its expiry on stderr; after it lapses, an acquire or control-plane upkeep serves the line.  An unhealthy host is never reserved: it stays free for the operator's verify or golden capture, whose successful release wakes the first waiter. Session end and execution settlement cancel every wait; releasing an unused reservation cancels that wait. When a released unused reservation was a waiting plan execution's last live wait, that execution is aborted in the same transaction as qa_host_turn_released, with the fresh yoke qa plan run that recovers it, so control-plane upkeep wakes its member instead of counting it as still walking. Before it parks, a queued plan runs and records every remaining host-free automatic case (Command without method_config.test_machine, Command (CI)) and names them in the park message; a failing one is recorded without leaving the line, and the cursor steps over recorded cases on resume. Machine cases, inherit chains and agent- or human-judged cases keep roster order. A rerun roster drops a passed case only when no later case of its chain still owes a verdict, so a chain always runs from its opener; at begin, a case whose review landed after the roster froze is recorded retained when it and the rest of its chain now pass, instead of blocking its followers as inherited_predecessor_not_passed. The claim_held refusal names the session's place in line, the holder's own release command, the steering-seat recovery and the park instruction. Declared-host Commands retain plan custody during local and nested host operations. Host-wait resume commands omit a global machine pin. Scheduling retains a previously used platform’s host from durable execution leases and runs; a new platform selects an eligible host independently. Member removal settles review executions immediately when every mission has already recorded its walk-end restore; unfinished walks retain custody for teardown. While its execution is live (active, waiting, walking or awaiting_walk_review), the holder's own release of a QA_HOST lease refuses qa_execution_holds_lease, naming the execution, its state, that the lease is released when the execution ends, and the yoke qa plan abort command for deliberate cancellation; the lease and execution stay as they were. Release by a steering seat, by claim id or by idle-hold upkeep aborts the owning execution with the release reason and releases every companion host atomically. Stop the runner and recover starting state before that release; custody loss never passes QA. The host-turn wake tells a waiter that no longer needs this turn to release it before taking it. A waiter whose process exits between turns is reported as waiting for its host turn (another_item, qa_host_turn_waiting, with holder item and position), not as a stalled session needing steering. A held QA_HOST lease whose session is parked, process-exited or ended, with no tool call, no subagent tool call (last_child_tool_call_at) and no recorded host operation on that lease for the machine setting qa_host_idle_hold_minutes (default 60; heartbeats and watcher pulses never count; a holder whose subagent called a tool within the limit is working, not away), is returned by control-plane upkeep: reservations of any host set still waiting on that host go back to waiting at their execution's place and serve their lines, then the lease is released through manual release, recording the reset owed and aborting the walk as qa_host_idle_hold_expired with the yoke qa plan run that starts it again; the next waiter is woken. A plan execution waiting for a host set whose session is parked, process-exited or ended with no tool call for that same limit keeps its place in every line but is passed over when a host is served while it still waits on another host; upkeep hands each partial reservation it already holds to the next waiter (qa_host_idle_waiters). Its next tool call ends the skip: the next release serves it at its place. A plan execution whose owning run has not opened its QA stage (a takeover moved it to a successor still before item QA) keeps its place in every line but is passed over when a host is served, and releasing a reservation already held for it returns the wait to waiting at its place instead of aborting it (qa_host_stage_unopened); when the stage opens, the stage-wait notice sends its owner to yoke qa plan run, which re-freezes the same execution and serves it at its original place.
desired: Live proof on a registered test host: a member plan started while the host is leased is queued and woken on release, then takes the turn; and a plan queued on an unhealthy host is woken by a successful golden capture, without a steerer notifying anyone by hand; and on a contended run a queued plan's host-free Command cases record before it parks and are not rerun on resume; and a plan whose lab host is stopped queues on ssh_unavailable and is woken after the operator starts the host and verify succeeds; and an aborted shared walk's recovery run resumes next on its host, ahead of unrelated waiters; and a standalone plan whose matrix case waits on a busy host keeps its first queued_at on every host while its one-host baseline holds only its own host; and on production with an empty Studio line, a preflight exec followed by another session's qa plan run and then the preflighter's case run gives the lease to the preflighter, with the hold-over named in the receipts.; and on a lab host a walk parked in awaiting_walk_review past qa_host_idle_hold_minutes is released with its reset owed recorded, the host set queued behind it keeps its place, and that second session is woken and walks; and on a lab host the holder of a reserved plan turn runs yoke test-machine reset, its claim stays held with its qa-host-turn: reason, and its yoke qa plan run then takes the host while a second session keeps waiting.
